name: La Troyenne
notes: Varied grades and climbing styles on this sector.
Rock quality ranges from poor to exceptional.
routes: Sustained with good rests; difficulty increases and is varied. Both technical and physical.
Delicate slab livened up by a curious mantel onto a glued block. Unusual climbing.
Direct variant of 138 straight up the slab. Consistent and sustained overall.
Original line with successive traverses that give this route a unique character. (Possible start via 140: 5c+.)
La dure réalité de la friction
Very nice route with fun tufa in the first part; some loose flakes at the top need care. A must-do!
Finishing variant of 140 (trend slightly right after the horizontal band).
Not consistent; a slightly reach-dependent roof move, but pleasant nonetheless.
Le cheval blanc aux oreilles bleues
The White Horse with Blue Ears
Sustained, varied and surprising climbing. A rather sneaky Cormot-style pillar.
Varied climbing that needs good route-reading and good anticipation of the line. A classic.
Sustained. Needs good reading (some holds are hidden). Nice technical climbing in the first part; the rest is rather athletic on good holds.
Sustained, continuous and varied. Physical start on edges, then a slab all about balance, a corner and a fun mantel. Loose rock on the last 2 metres. Nice route.
Pump galore. Not easy onsight — reading and determination are essential weapons for this route. Very fun overhanging pillar.
Direct variant of 149. Bouldery. Demanding technical climbing.
Route with an original line. Start with a traverse under a small roof, then a traversing line. The rock sometimes has no texture, so you have to squeeze the holds all the harder.
Finishing variant of 149. Traverse all the way left to finish on the left face. Move over a big wedged block, great atmosphere.
Slightly bouldery but original route. The finish on the side of the prow may leave you with a few souvenirs.
Traverses slightly left, on good holds. The rock is loose at the top — careful with some unstable blocks.
Historic but inconsistent route, broken up by ledges. Demanding and very aesthetic summit overhang.
Sustained, varied climbing. Sneaky, demanding exit slab. Slightly loose rock at the top below the anchor.
Starting variant of 153. Technical finger climbing.
